[[Category:Activation function]]
[[File:ReLU-LeakyReLU-ELU-activation-functions.svg|thumbnail|ReLU (solid), Leaky ReLU ($\alpha=0.1$ dashed, $\alpha=0.01$ dotted) and ELU ($\alpha=1$, dash-dotted) for $z\in[-4,4]$]]
''' (Leaky) rectified/exponential linear units''' is a family of [[activation function]]s designed to normalise negative [[artificial neuron#Layer composition|pre-activation values]].

== Rectified linear unit (ReLU) ==

$$
\operatorname{ReLU}(z)=\max(0,z).
$$

ReLU, which simply set any negative values to $0$, is the cheapest activation function in compute.

However, since

$$
\frac{\partial \operatorname{ReLU}(z)}{\partial z}=0 \quad \text{for } z<0
$$

A potential probelm can arise during training via [[backpropagation]] if $z_i<0$ for most or all [[artificial neuron]]s in a given layer $l$:

$$
\frac{\partial \operatorname{ReLU}(\vec z_l)}{\partial \vec z_l} \to 0
$$

preventing efficient backpropagation.

In extreme cases, once $\forall z_i \in \vec z_l: z_i<0$, backpropagation completely stops updating the weights and bias of the layer, making the layer effectively a '''dead unit''' that

* does nothing during [[forward pass]];
* cannot be recovered via standard [[backpropagation]].

== Leaky ReLU ==

To '''prevent''' the rise of '''dead units''' with standard ReLU, the leaky version introduces a small slope $1 \ll \alpha>0$ (e.g., $0.01$ in [[PyTorch]] by default),

$$
\operatorname{LeakyReLU}(z)=
\begin{cases}
z, & z\ge 0,\\
\alpha z, & z<0.
\end{cases}
$$

normalising $z<0$ towards $0$ without risking dead units.

== Exponential linear unit (ELU) ==

For $\alpha>0$ (e.g., $\alpha=1$ in [[Tensorflow]] by default),

$$
\operatorname{ELU}(z)=
\begin{cases}
z, & z>0,\\
\alpha\left(e^{z}-1\right), & z\le 0.
\end{cases}
$$

which is

* smoother than Leaky ReLU near $z=0$
* numerically stabler: outputs mean activations closer to zero
